additional_requirements: The binge eating and inappropriate compensatory behaviors both occur, on average, at least once a week for 3 months

S045.name: Fear_of_Weight_Gain
S045.description: Intense fear of gaining weight or of becoming fat, even though at a significantly low weight.

subtypes.Fear of Weight Gain: Extreme fear and loathing of gaining weight or becoming fat.
subtypes.Fear of Specific Foods: Fear that eating high-calorie foods will immediately lead to weight gain.
subtypes.Obsession with Weight Gain: Compulsively checking the scale and becoming extremely anxious about even the slightest increase.

S047.name: Compensatory_Behavior_NonPurging
S047.description: Recurrent inappropriate compensatory behaviors to prevent weight gain without purging (direct removal of food).

subtypes.Fasting: Intentionally stopping food intake for a certain period to prevent weight gain.
subtypes.Excessive Exercise: Repetitively performing exercise at a level that exceeds physical limits to prevent weight gain.

S048.name: Compensatory_Behavior_Purging
S048.description: Recurrent inappropriate compensatory behaviors involving the expulsion of food or fluids to prevent weight gain.

subtypes.Self-Induced Vomiting: Intentionally inducing vomiting to remove ingested food.
subtypes.Misuse of Medications: Repetitively misusing laxatives, diuretics, or enemas for the purpose of weight control.

S049.name: Eating_Large_Amount
S049.description: Eating, in a discrete period of time, an amount of food that is definitely larger than what most individuals would eat in a similar period of time under similar circumstances.
examples: Eating more than 3-4 times the amount of a typical meal within 2 hours.
Continuously eating large amounts of high-calorie snacks in addition to main meals.
Eating enough to empty a significant portion of the refrigerator or pantry at once.
Eating clearly more food than others during the same period of time.

S050.name: Loss_of_Control
S050.description: A sense of lack of control over eating during the episode (e.g., a feeling that one cannot stop eating or control what or how much one is eating).
examples: A feeling that once I start eating, I cannot stop even if I want to.
Thinking 'I shouldn't eat any more' but mechanically continuing to eat.
A feeling of helplessness that I cannot decide for myself how much to eat.
Eating as if my body is being controlled by someone else.

symptom.disease_info: Bulimia nervosa is characterized by recurrent episodes of binge eating accompanied by a sense of loss of control, followed by inappropriate compensatory behaviors such as self-induced vomiting, misuse of laxatives/diuretics, fasting, or excessive exercise to prevent weight gain. Individuals typically have an overvaluation of body shape and weight, but unlike anorexia nervosa, body weight is usually in the normal or overweight range, which can delay recognition by others. The course is often chronic or relapsing, with symptoms waxing and waning in response to stress, interpersonal difficulties, and changes in routine or role demands. Clinically, it must be distinguished from binge-eating disorder (which lacks regular compensatory behaviors) and from normal dieting or occasional overeating by its frequency, loss of control, and impact on psychosocial functioning and health.

patient.stressor: Around 17 months ago, Linda’s youngest child moved out and her husband shifted to partial retirement, leaving her household routines and sense of daily purpose markedly changed. With more unstructured time and a quieter home, she began oscillating between busy spurts of quilting, gardening, and sorority work and stretches of late‑evening TV and road‑trip snacking, all while becoming more self‑conscious about age‑related body changes and her image as a health professional in her community. What started as casual comfort eating during lonely evenings gradually turned into secretive episodes around food, followed by drastic attempts to "get back on track" before church gatherings or sorority events. She finally agreed to see a psychiatrist after her primary‑care doctor noticed a pattern of weight fluctuation and lab abnormalities during an annual visit and gently questioned how much control she felt she had over her eating.
patient.chief_complaint: When I start eating, especially in the evenings, I feel like I lose control and can’t seem to stop myself.

S045.name: Fear_of_Weight_Gain
S045.description: Intense fear of gaining weight or of becoming fat, even though at a significantly low weight.
S045.manifestation: Even though my doctors say my weight is fine for my age, if the scale is even two pounds higher than last week I panic and start replaying every bite I’ve eaten, convinced I’m on this slippery slope to getting fat and people at church or at the office judging me for it.

S047.name: Compensatory_Behavior_NonPurging
S047.description: Recurrent inappropriate compensatory behaviors to prevent weight gain without purging (direct removal of food).
S047.manifestation: To make up for what I eat, I’ll skip breakfast and sometimes lunch the next day and force myself to walk on the treadmill or do laps around the neighborhood until my knees ache, telling myself I don’t deserve dinner if I don’t ‘burn off’ last night’s binge.

S048.name: Compensatory_Behavior_Purging
S048.description: Recurrent inappropriate compensatory behaviors involving the expulsion of food or fluids to prevent weight gain.
S048.manifestation: More nights than I want to admit, after I’ve eaten way too much in front of the TV, I sneak into the bathroom, run the water for cover, and make myself throw up or take extra laxatives so I feel like I’ve erased the damage before anyone notices my weight creeping up.

S049.name: Eating_Large_Amount
S049.description: Eating, in a discrete period of time, an amount of food that is definitely larger than what most individuals would eat in a similar period of time under similar circumstances.
S049.manifestation: On those lonely evenings when my husband goes to bed early, I’ll sit in the kitchen and go through half a loaf of bread with butter, a big bowl of cereal, leftover casserole, and whatever snacks are in the pantry in less than an hour, long past the point of feeling physically sick but somehow still reaching for more.

S050.name: Loss_of_Control
S050.description: A sense of lack of control over eating during the episode (e.g., a feeling that one cannot stop eating or control what or how much one is eating).
S050.manifestation: Once I start picking at something in the evening—maybe just a few chips or a slice of cheese—it’s like a switch flips and I’m suddenly raiding every cupboard, telling myself to stop but watching my hands keep grabbing and eating until I feel stuffed and ashamed, like I wasn’t really the one in charge.
